title: Edith Stein: The Seventh Chamber
text: A Hungarian-Polish drama about the Jewish philosopher who became a Carmelite and died at Auschwitz. Edith Stein was beatified in 1987 and canonised in 1998.

title: Life for Life: Maximilian Kolbe
text: A drama about the Franciscan who gave his life for another prisoner at Auschwitz. Maximilian Kolbe was beatified in 1971 and canonised in 1982.

title: Molokai: The Story of Father Damien
text: A drama about the Belgian priest who served the leper colony on Molokai. Damien was beatified in 1995 and canonised in 2009.

title: Poveda
text: A Spanish biographical film about the priest and educator Pedro Poveda, killed in 1936. He was beatified in 1993 and canonised in 2003.

title: Our God's Brother
text: A Polish film about the painter who gave up art to serve the poor as Brother Albert. Albert Chmielowski was beatified in 1983 and canonised in 1989.

title: A Forbidden God
text: A Spanish film about the Claretian seminarians martyred at Barbastro in 1936. The martyrs were beatified in 1992.

title: For Greater Glory
text: A large-scale drama of the Cristero War in Mexico, with Andy García and Peter O'Toole. Its young martyr José Sánchez del Río was beatified in 2005 and canonised in 2016.

title: A Hidden Life
text: Malick's film about Franz Jägerstätter, the Austrian farmer who refused the oath to Hitler and was executed. He was beatified in 2007.

title: Triumph of the Heart
text: A recent American drama about Maximilian Kolbe and his sacrifice at Auschwitz. Kolbe was beatified in 1971 and canonised in 1982.

title: Rome, Open City
text: Rossellini's landmark film of the Resistance in occupied Rome. Its centre is the Resistance, not the faith, and it presents a priest's common cause with Communist partisans as exemplary, against Pius XI's Divini Redemptoris. It is not Catholic-centred.

title: Léon Morin, Priest
text: Melville's drama of a young priest and a widow in wartime France. The film's moral centre, Father Morin, says that an atheist is not damned and that God is Catholic only in our language, an invisible-Church view Pius XII rejected in Mystici Corporis and Humani generis.

title: Men of Boys Town
text: The sequel to Boys Town, again with Father Flanagan as lead. Its subject is abuse in a state reformatory and the fight to pay off Boys Town's debts. Its religion is a generic faith, and Flanagan's stated ideal is a place for boys of every creed.

title: Of Gods and Men
text: A Cannes Grand Prix winner about the Trappist monks of Tibhirine, killed in Algeria. Its Catholic content is the post-conciliar Church presented as normal and exemplary: the community's interreligious witness, ending in a testament that speaks of Islam in the language of post-conciliar dialogue.

title: On the Waterfront
text: A classic crime drama with Catholic characters and setting. Father Barry's waterfront ministry and his sermon are real and well drawn, but the film is centred on Terry Malloy's testimony against a corrupt union. Faith is one strand of the story, not its subject.

title: The Agony and the Ecstasy
text: A lavish film of Michelangelo and Pope Julius II. The papal court is the setting, but the subject is an artist's struggle with his patron over the Sistine ceiling. Faith appears as Michelangelo's private idea of God, and the pope is shown humbled by it.

title: The Sound of Music
text: The famous musical about Maria and the von Trapp family. The abbey frames Maria's discernment respectfully, but the film is a family romance and an escape story. Catholic life is the setting rather than the subject, and the real family's chaplain is written out.

title: Brother Orchid
text: A gangster comedy with Edward G. Robinson, in which the hero hides among flower-growing brothers. Their order is invented, and no Mass, sacrament, doctrine or Church authority appears. Religious life is comic colour, not the subject.

title: Jesus of Nazareth
text: Zeffirelli's widely watched television life of Christ. It was shaped by Nostra Aetate, and that conciliar reading is built into the drama: an invented scribe engineers the arrest and Judas is a well-meaning dupe, shifting the Gospel account of responsibility.

title: Saint Teresa of the Andes
text: A Chilean production about the young Carmelite who died in 1920. Teresa of the Andes was beatified in 1987 and canonised in 1993.

title: Padre Pio: Miracle Man
text: An Italian television miniseries about the Capuchin stigmatist of San Giovanni Rotondo. Padre Pio was canonised only in 2002.

title: St. Giuseppe Moscati: Doctor to the Poor
text: An Italian television production about the Neapolitan physician who cared for the poor. Giuseppe Moscati was beatified in 1975 and canonised in 1987.

title: Bakhita: From Slave to Saint
text: An Italian television production about the Sudanese slave who became a Canossian sister. Josephine Bakhita was beatified in 1992 and canonised in 2000.

title: Restless Heart: The Confessions of Augustine
text: The shortened English-language edition of an Italian miniseries on St Augustine. It invents a massacre at Ambrose's basilica as the immediate cause of his conversion, displacing the struggle of mind and will in the Confessions. The judgment concerns this edition, not the full miniseries.

title: Mother Teresa
text: A television film on the life of the foundress of the Missionaries of Charity. Mother Teresa was beatified in 2003 and canonised in 2016.

title: Padre Pio: Between Heaven and Earth
text: An Italian television miniseries about the Capuchin stigmatist. Padre Pio was canonised only in 2002.

title: Blessed Duns Scotus: Defender of the Immaculate Conception
text: An Italian film about the medieval Franciscan theologian. John Duns Scotus received the title Blessed only when his cult was confirmed in 1993.

title: Into Great Silence
text: A prize-winning, wordless documentary on the Grande Chartreuse. Its Catholic content is the post-conciliar Church presented as normal: the monastery as it lives today, after the Carthusians' post-conciliar revision of their liturgy.

title: No Greater Love
text: A documentary on the daily life of a Carmelite community in Baltimore. It is a sincere portrait, but it shows a present-day convent filmed in 2009, the post-conciliar Church presented as the ordinary Church.

title: Two Crowns
text: A documentary about Maximilian Kolbe and his sacrifice at Auschwitz. Kolbe was beatified in 1971 and canonised in 1982.

title: Faith of Our Fathers: In Search of the English Martyrs
text: A documentary tour of the sites of recusant England. The history is sound and well located, but serving post-conciliar bishops speak as the authorities throughout, and the film celebrates the 1970 canonisations as the culmination of the martyrs' story.

title: Finding Fátima
text: A documentary on the Fátima apparitions. The 1917 material is sound, but the climax is the post-conciliar Church: it presents John Paul II's survival in 1981 and the Vatican's 2000 reading of the third secret as the fulfilment of Fátima.

title: Guadalupe: Mother of Humanity
text: A documentary on Our Lady of Guadalupe. Half of it is present-day testimony, with post-conciliar clergy as its authorities, and it makes claims about the tilma, including music in its proportions, that the Church has never endorsed. The 1531 account is not its centre.

title: Saint Pio of Pietrelcina: Man of Hope and Healing
text: A recent docudrama on Padre Pio. He was canonised only in 2002.

title: Silence
text: Scorsese's adaptation of Endō's novel on Jesuits in Japan. At the climax a voice presented as Christ's tells the priest to trample His image, and the final image honours a hidden faith after public apostasy. This contradicts the duty to confess the faith under persecution.

title: The Two Popes
text: A fictional conversation between Benedict XVI and the future Francis. Detailed criticism finds an invented conflict built on a false resignation chronology, a caricature of tradition against progress, and an ending that promotes contemporary reform. It is not claimed to be condemned by the Church.

title: Conclave
text: A fictional papal-election thriller that won wide praise for its craft. Its resolution argues for change in Catholic teaching, as secular and Catholic critics agree, ending with the election of a pope who is a woman, contrary to the Church's teaching on holy orders.

title: Brother Sun, Sister Moon
text: Zeffirelli's lyrical life of St Francis. It recasts him as a counter-cultural figure of the 1970s, makes the bishop and papal court the antagonists, and shows vernacular worship, with the priest facing the people, as the purified Church.

title: Cabrini
text: A well-made film about the foundress who served Italian immigrants in New York. Catholic critics find it almost without religious language or prayer, with the saint's motive turned into self-determination and the hierarchy cast as antagonist.

title: Fátima
text: A feature film on the 1917 apparitions. Our Lady's words are reworked, and the request about Russia and the consecration is left out, so the film misrepresents the message it claims to tell. It adds an invented 1989 frame with a sceptical interviewer.

title: The Exorcist
text: The famous horror film of a possessed girl and two priests. Its force depends on extended obscene and sacrilegious material, including a desecrated crucifix and church, which its Jesuit adviser protested. It is not claimed to be condemned, but no edition can be recommended without grave reservation.

title: The Day of the Siege: September Eleven 1683
text: A film of the relief of Vienna in 1683. It is built around the Capuchin Marco d'Aviano, first-billed, with a miraculous healing credited to him. He was beatified only in 2003.

title: Calvary
text: A dark Irish drama in which a good priest is threatened with murder. Its Catholic content is a present-day Irish parish and its priest, the post-conciliar Church presented as the ordinary Church.

title: The Tree of Life
text: Malick's Palme d'Or winner, centred on a Texas family in the 1950s. The family goes to church, but Catholic faith, worship and sacraments are not its subject. Its religion is a general meditation on grace and nature, framed by the Book of Job.

title: Au revoir les enfants
text: A fine film about a boy's friendship with a hidden Jewish classmate at a Carmelite school. The headmaster-priest is heroic, but the subject is the friendship, a betrayal and lost innocence. Catholic life is the setting, not the subject.

title: Romero
text: A drama about the Archbishop of San Salvador, killed at the altar in 1980. Óscar Romero was beatified in 2015 and canonised in 2018.

title: Faustina
text: A Polish film about the Polish nun of the Divine Mercy devotion. Faustina Kowalska was beatified in 1993 and canonised in 2000.

title: Pedro Calungsod: Batang Martir
text: A Filipino film about the young catechist martyred in Guam in 1672. Pedro Calungsod was beatified in 2000 and canonised in 2012.

title: Padre Cícero: Os Milagres de Juazeiro
text: A Brazilian film about the priest of Juazeiro, suspended by the Church after a disputed miracle that the Holy See refused to recognise. It centres on the Church's inquiries and sides with him against Church authority, ending in his expulsion and persecution.

title: Nazarín
text: Buñuel's film of Galdós's Christ-like priest. The director, an atheist, uses him to argue that literal Christian charity is futile and that the Church disowns it, inventing scenes the novel lacks. Its ambiguity nearly won an OCIC prize, but the thesis stands.

title: The Dark Night
text: Saura's film of St John of the Cross in prison. It invents a sin tied to a lustful nun, casts the same actress as the Virgin Mary, and stages the soul's union with the Bridegroom as an erotic kiss. Saura called his subject a secular mysticism.

title: A Man Escaped
text: Bresson's escape drama has a real spiritual dimension, with a Gospel verse passed to the hero and the Kyrie of Mozart's Mass in C minor. But no sacrament or Catholic practice is at its centre, and the cleric among the prisoners is a Protestant pastor.

title: Au Hasard Balthazar
text: Bresson's parable of a donkey passed from owner to owner. Its Christian meaning is implicit and allegorical, and Catholic practice appears only in passing. A girl's sexual abuse is part of the story. Its 1966 OCIC award is post-conciliar and does not change this.

title: Black Narcissus
text: A celebrated film of nuns in a Himalayan convent. The sisters are an Anglican order, not Catholic. The Legion of Decency also condemned it for presenting the convent as an escape for the neurotic, lifting the condemnation only after cuts.

title: Daens
text: A Belgian film about the priest Adolf Daens and the textile workers of Aalst. It presents his persistence in party politics against his bishop and the Pope as heroic, and the Church as siding with the factory owners against the workers.

title: Dead Man Walking
text: A death-row drama with Susan Sarandon as Sister Helen Prejean. Its Catholic content is a post-conciliar sister's apostolate, shown as exemplary. Its moral frame is opposition to the death penalty, which the Roman Catechism admits as lawful.

title: Dekalog
text: Ten television films using the Commandments as loose starting points for moral dilemmas on a Warsaw housing estate. Kieślowski said they do not match the Commandments exactly. Faith and sacraments are not central, and affairs, abortion and murder have no Catholic resolution.

title: Doubt
text: A parable set in a Bronx school in 1964, while the Council sat. A severe traditional nun is set against a progressive priest who stands for the reforms. The film honours doubt over certainty, and the nun's certainty collapses at the end.

title: Europe '51
text: Rossellini's drama of a bourgeois woman who turns to charity after a tragedy. She works out a private Christianity outside the Church, and every institution, the Church included, rejects her. It is not Catholic-centred, and its thesis sets sanctity apart from the Church.

title: Hail Mary
text: Godard's modern-dress retelling of the Annunciation and Virgin Birth. It shows the Mary figure in repeated nudity and ends on her sexual self-exploration. John Paul II said it deeply wounds believers' religious sentiments, and it was banned in Argentina and Brazil.

title: Jesus
text: A Gospel of Luke film financed and distributed by Campus Crusade for Christ as a missionary tool. The drama is unobjectionable in itself, but it closes with an on-screen sinner's prayer inviting the viewer to accept Christ as personal Saviour, a Protestant evangelistic purpose.

title: Jesus Christ Superstar
text: The film of the rock opera. Its authors see Jesus through Judas's eyes as a mere man, and it ends at the death on the cross with no Resurrection. Catholic objections also noted a line making the bread only possibly His body.

title: The Nun
text: Rivette's adaptation of Diderot's anticlerical novel. A girl forced into vows is persecuted by one superior, pursued by another, refused release by the Church, and ends in a brothel and suicide. Catholic bodies condemned it as blasphemous, and it was briefly banned in France.

title: Lourdes
text: A prize-winning film about a wheelchair user on an Order of Malta pilgrimage to Lourdes. It shows the post-conciliar Church as the ordinary Church, and its ironic agnosticism leaves the cure in doubt, neither defending the miraculous nor the pre-conciliar faith.

title: Mother Joan of the Angels
text: A Polish film of the possessed nuns of Loudun. It presents the Church's exorcism as powerless, and its climax treats a priest's axe-murder of two men, done to take the prioress's demons on himself, as a sacrifice. The thesis is heterodox and anticlerical.

title: Mouchette
text: Bresson's adaptation of Bernanos, following a destitute girl who is raped and then drowns herself. Faith, sacraments and clergy are not its subject, and the suicide closes the film with no counterweight. Its 1967 OCIC prize is post-conciliar.

title: Keeper of Promises
text: The Brazilian Palme d'Or winner, also known as O Pagador de Promessas. It sets a syncretic Candomblé vow against a rigid, intolerant priest and ends with the cross forced into the church. It is read as an indictment of the Church, and an archdiocesan paper warned the faithful against it.

title: Silence
text: Shinoda's earlier Japanese film of Endō's novel. Its climax is the Jesuit Rodrigo's apostasy at the fumie, and it goes further than Endō: the apostate ends as a samurai with a dead man's wife and name, an ending Endō himself disliked.

title: Simon of the Desert
text: Buñuel's short satire on St Simeon Stylites. It shows his asceticism as egotism, his miracles as futile and the monks as hypocrites, and ends with the Devil carrying him off to a 1960s New York nightclub. Church hypocrisy and dogma are its targets.

title: Stations of the Cross
text: A German drama in fourteen shots about a girl in a family attached to a traditionalist society modelled on the SSPX. Its thesis is that traditional Catholic practice is dangerous: priest and mother are shown as the cause of her fatal self-sacrifice.

title: The Last Temptation of Christ
text: Scorsese's adaptation of Kazantzakis. It disclaims the Gospels as its basis and shows Christ on the cross led by a false angel into a vision of marriage, consummated on screen, with Mary Magdalene and family life. It is blasphemous in content.

title: The Messenger: The Story of Joan of Arc
text: Besson's spectacle on St Joan. It invents a childhood trauma to drive her, and in prison an allegorical Conscience leads her to doubt her visions came from God. It is a sceptical thesis about a saint's divine mission, with graphic violence.

title: The Shoes of the Fisherman
text: A Hollywood drama of a Russian pope, with Anthony Quinn. The exemplary pope befriends a Teilhard-like theologian, prays a Jewish prayer at a deathbed as dialogue, and pledges the Church's wealth. These 1960s gestures are presented as the ideal of the papacy.

title: The Sign of the Cross
text: DeMille's martyr drama of Nero's Rome, one of the films that provoked the Legion of Decency campaign. The circulating restored version has an erotic dance meant to seduce the Christian heroine, a nude milk bath and arena scenes, impurity staged as spectacle.

title: Agnes of God
text: A film set in a convent, in which a novice's claim of a virgin conception is treated as a case for psychiatry and hypnosis. The investigation points to a human explanation, leaves a parody of the Incarnation open, and frames religious life as repression.

title: Brides of Christ
text: An Australian miniseries about a Sydney teaching order. It shows the conciliar upheaval as overdue change: a young nun wants to drop practices that have lost their meaning, a nun falls in love with a liberal priest, and students are urged to question the hierarchy.

title: Cardinal Lambertini
text: An Italian historical comedy with Gino Cervi as the future Benedict XIV in 1739 Bologna. The cardinal is the hero, a shrewd mediator who foils a plot and helps two lovers marry, but the film's matter is political intrigue and romance, not the faith.

title: Change of Habit
text: An Elvis Presley film in which three sisters put off the habit to work incognito in a ghetto clinic. It includes a folk-song Mass led by Presley, and presents religious life as reformed after the Council, with the new liturgy, as the norm.

title: Clare
text: An Italian film of St Clare of Assisi, shown at Venice. Reviewers read its thesis as anticlerical: the Church, embodied by Cardinal Ugolino, is contemptuous patriarchy, enclosure is lost freedom, and the community is a hierarchy-free commune.

title: An Ardent Heart
text: A Spanish documentary on devotion to the Sacred Heart. The devotion is pre-conciliar, but it is told through Bernardo de Hoyos, beatified in 2010, and the Divine Mercy shrine of St Faustina, canonised in 2000, alongside present-day testimonies.

title: Corpus Christi
text: An Oscar-nominated Polish drama of a young ex-convict who poses as a priest. It presents his sacrilegious simulation of confession and Mass sympathetically, as more alive than the institutional priesthood, and includes a sexual encounter and drug use.

title: Joan of Arc
text: A German film, also known as Das Mädchen Johanna, rated state-valuable under the Nazi regime. It recasts St Joan inside a leadership myth: Charles VII uses her as a tool and decides she must burn, and her sanctity is subordinated to politics.

title: The Gaucho Priest
text: An Argentine film about Fr José Gabriel Brochero, played by Enrique Muiño. He was beatified in 2013 and canonised in 2016, after the Council, so the rule applies although the film itself dates from 1941.

title: Entertaining Angels: The Dorothy Day Story
text: A 1996 Paulist production on Dorothy Day. Her conversion and the Catholic Worker are pre-conciliar, but the frame is post-conciliar social-justice Catholicism, it shows her pre-conversion abortion, and it stages her clash with a bishop.

title: Fátima
text: A drama following women on a pilgrimage to Fátima. The director, who is not a believer, has said it began as a study of group dynamics and is about a need for some faith, not necessarily Catholic. The quarrels matter more than the doctrine, so the faith is not the subject.

title: Fatima: The Ultimate Mystery
text: A documentary on Fátima whose voices are post-conciliar churchmen and whose climax reads the apparitions through John Paul II's survival of the 1981 attack. The post-conciliar Church is presented as the apparitions' fulfilment.

title: Francesco
text: Cavani's second film on St Francis. It attributes his conversion to a forbidden vernacular Gospel, implying Church opposition, shows worldly prelates, and gives Clare feelings beyond the saintly. Critics such as Steven Greydanus call its picture of his spirituality gravely misguided. It offers a humanist reinterpretation of the saint.

title: Francis of Assisi
text: Cavani's television film drew on Paul Sabatier's Protestant life of Francis, which was placed on the Index. It shows him as a protester standing outside the Church's rules, with miracles and mysticism removed and his conversion read as social rebellion. Its thesis sets the saint against the Church.

title: Garabandal, Only God Knows
text: A documentary advocating the alleged apparitions at Garabandal. The bishops of Santander held them unproven from 1961 and declared in 1967 that they had not occurred. The film sets itself against that judgment, and the apparitions have never been approved.

title: Gospa
text: A drama on the Medjugorje phenomenon, which began in 1981. The Church has never approved the alleged apparitions, and its hero, Fr Jozo Zovko, was later deprived of his faculties by the local bishop. The whole film is built on the claim that they are authentic.

title: Guadalupe
text: The apparitions of 1531 appear as flashbacks inside a present-day drama about two Spanish archaeologists, framed by a modern pilgrimage and a panel of experts. Juan Diego himself was beatified in 1990 and canonised in 2002.

title: I, the Worst of All
text: A well-made film on Sor Juana Inés de la Cruz. It presents her as a feminist victim of a misogynist hierarchy, reads her bond with the Vicereine as an unspoken love, and frames her final penance as the breaking of her spirit. Its thesis is anticlerical.

title: The Messiah
text: Rossellini's last film keeps the Gospel words of divinity, but every miracle happens off screen, the prophecy of the Resurrection is cut, and it ends on the empty tomb. Its Christ is reduced to the perfect man, as Rossellini intended and as its Catholic co-producer, Fr Patrick Peyton, objected.

title: In the Name of the Pope King
text: A drama of papal Rome in 1867, shown as a decrepit regime that sends revolutionaries to the scaffold. Its hero, a papal judge, breaks with the Church's authorities and ends by refusing Communion to the General of the Jesuits. The film argues an anticlerical case against the temporal power.

title: Jacinta
text: Jacinta Marto, one of the Fátima children, was recognised as blessed only in 2000 and canonised in 2017.

title: Jeromin
text: Adapted from Fr Luis Coloma's novel, the film covers the boyhood of Don John of Austria. Its subject is his hidden royal birth and patriotic promise. A Catholic upbringing gives the story colour, but the faith is not its subject.

title: Jesus
text: A Catholic-produced life of Christ that keeps the Passion and Resurrection. But Christ seems unsure of his mission until his mother pushes him, the Baptist asks him to confess his sins, and visions of the Crusades are offered as a case against the Cross. It closes with Christ in modern dress.

title: Jesus of Montreal
text: A celebrated film in which actors stage a Passion play. It makes Christ the son of a Roman soldier who seduced Mary, drawing on historical-Jesus scholarship. The Church authorities who stop the play are the antagonists, and an organ donation stands in for the Resurrection.

title: Keepers of the Night
text: An ecumenical German film, the first postwar one made with the money and ideas of the Protestant Church. Its protagonist is a Protestant pastor, with a Catholic chaplain as his equal partner. The faith is shown as one among others, and the film leaves a doubter's return to belief open.

title: The Apparition
text: A respectful French drama about a journalist asked to investigate a young woman's claimed apparition, within the present-day Church. It stays orthodox where it touches doctrine but is agnostic about the event. The apparition it investigates is modern and unapproved.

title: Faith
text: A Spanish drama of a young priest's doubts and a girl's false accusation. Some read it as an exaltation of the priesthood. But Cardinal Segura of Seville forbade it under pain of mortal sin and the Bishop of Barcelona warned the faithful against it, and their judgment outweighs its adult rating.

title: The Last Summit
text: A documentary on a Spanish priest ordained and formed after the Council, with present-day priests, bishops and seminary students as witnesses. It presents the diocesan priesthood of today as exemplary, which makes the post-conciliar Church its frame.

title: Brother André
text: André Bessette was beatified in 1982 and canonised in 2010.

title: Free
text: A documentary on contemplative life in twelve Spanish monasteries, as the communities stand. It presents that life as exemplary and frames it with Pope Francis's description of contemplatives as lighthouses for our time.

title: Lorenzo Ruiz: The Saint... A Filipino
text: Lorenzo Ruiz was beatified in 1981 and canonised in 1987.

title: Mary, Mother of Jesus
text: A television film that rewrites the Gospel to make Mary more suitable for our time. Joseph rejects her in anger, she teaches the boy Jesus his parables, she is baptised by John, and James is Jesus's younger brother, which on its face denies her perpetual virginity.

title: Mass Appeal
text: A comedy-drama with Jack Lemmon about a popular pastor and a seminarian. It presents the post-conciliar parish and seminary as normal, and sides with the seminarian who challenges his pastor on women's ordination and the expulsion of two seminarians. The pastor ends by taking his side.

title: Miracle at Moreaux
text: A convent school and a nun hide three Jewish children in wartime France. The drama concerns the rescue and the pupils' prejudice, and it resolves as the Jewish children teach their Catholic classmates about Judaism. The Nativity pageant is background, so the faith is not the subject.

title: Molokai
text: Fr Damien de Veuster was beatified in 1995 and canonised in 2009. The film's 1959 date and Spanish awards do not change that.

title: Peter and Paul
text: A two-part television drama on the Apostles. Peter's martyrdom and the Petrine texts are there, but James rules at the Council of Jerusalem, Peter calls himself a failure replaced by Paul, and Paul preaches salvation through faith alone. Petrine primacy is denied in substance.

title: Pope John Paul II
text: John Paul II was beatified in 2011. Its second half also presents the post-conciliar papacy from 1978 to 2005 as exemplary.

title: Popiełuszko: Freedom Is Within Us
text: Fr Jerzy Popiełuszko was beatified only in 2010. The film also takes the post-conciliar Church of 1980s Poland as its setting.

title: Father's Dilemma
text: A comedy by Blasetti and Zavattini in which a girl's First Communion is the occasion for her father's Easter-morning misadventures. Its concern is human selfishness and generosity, not the sacrament. The Legion of Decency also rated it B for suggestive sequences.

title: Prophet
text: Cardinal Stefan Wyszyński was beatified only in 2021. The film also presents him as the discoverer of Karol Wojtyła.

title: The Primate: Three Years Out of a Thousand
text: This film on Cardinal Stefan Wyszyński's imprisonment honours a man who was beatified only in 2021.

title: Seven Cities of Gold
text: Fr Junípero Serra was beatified in 1988 and canonised in 2015. The Legion of Decency rated the film A-I and it dates from 1955, but the rule looks at when the subject was raised to the altars.

title: Sister Citroën
text: A slapstick Spanish comedy about an impulsive nun who learns to drive the convent's Citroën 2CV and collects alms for an orphanage. Religious life is the setting for traffic gags. No vocation, sacrament or doctrine is at its centre.

title: The Conversation
text: Archbishop Alojzije Stepinac was beatified in 1998.

title: The Silent Witness
text: A documentary on the Shroud of Turin. It is Catholic in subject, but its witnesses are forensic scientists, American researchers and the Anglican John Robinson, and it speaks of what Christians call the Resurrection. The Church's own judgment on the Shroud is not discussed.

title: The Third Miracle
text: A drama of a priest investigating a candidate for sainthood in the American Church of 1979. It shows the reformed canonisation procedure and parish life as the normal Church. The doubting, hard-drinking priest's romance is treated sympathetically, and the film is rated R for a brief simulated sex act.

title: The Trapp Family
text: The German film that preceded The Sound of Music. It is more openly Catholic than the musical, with Nonnberg Abbey and Fr Wasner in the story. But it remains a family story of a governess, a marriage, a choir and flight from the Nazis, and the faith is the setting.

title: Mary's Land
text: A documentary of present-day conversion testimonies, centred on Medjugorje, which the local bishops have never recognised. The director calls it a turning point for himself and his family. It presents the unapproved apparition as a source of grace without qualification.

title: To Kill a Priest
text: The priest is renamed Father Alek, but the film is openly based on the 1984 murder of Fr Jerzy Popiełuszko, who was beatified only in 2010.

title: Where Angels Go, Trouble Follows
text: A comedy sequel to The Trouble with Angels. A conservative Mother Superior and a progressive young nun take pupils to an ecumenical youth rally, where the sisters resolve their differences and swap habits for short skirts. Post-conciliar renewal and ecumenism are the film's ideal.

title: A Time for Miracles
text: A television life of Elizabeth Seton, who was beatified in 1963. The story is framed by her 1975 canonisation inquiry and closes on footage of Paul VI. The post-conciliar Church is therefore the film's interpretive frame, not a passing coda.

title: The Christian Revolt
text: Ōshima's film on the Shimabara rising of persecuted Japanese Christians in 1637-38. Festival archives describe it as a cautionary tale on subverting authority and a metaphor for 1960s political repression. The faith is the vehicle for an allegory of armed revolt.

title: Anchieta, José do Brasil
text: The Jesuit missionary José de Anchieta was beatified in 1980 and canonised in 2014.

title: Cardinal Lambertini
text: A historical comedy in which Cardinal Lambertini, the future Benedict XIV, mediates between Spanish occupiers and resentful nobles in Bologna. The cardinal is the hero, but the matter is political intrigue and comedy, not the faith.

title: Close to Heaven
text: Commissioned by Catholic Action, the film shows Bishop Anselmo Polanco of Teruel refusing to leave, then imprisoned and executed in 1939. He was beatified only in 1995.

title: Damien: The Leper Priest
text: Fr Damien was declared Venerable in 1977, beatified in 1995 and canonised in 2009.

title: Anyway, Juan Is Your Name
text: A Mexican film on the Cristero War seen from the side of a federal general who jails priests and represses the people. Reference summaries say it severely criticises the Catholic Church. The persecutor is its centre, and the Church is its target.

title: The Priest from Kirchfeld
text: Adapted from Anzengruber's anticlerical play, written against clerical celibacy, the ban on mixed marriages and papal infallibility. Its priest loves his ward and wins respect by burying a suicide in consecrated ground against Church law. Defiance of discipline is its moral centre.

title: The Priest from Kirchfeld
text: This remake of Anzengruber's anticlerical play sides with the priest's disobedience to his bishop. He secretly marries a couple whom the diocese refused, and his transfer is framed as an injustice. He keeps his vow, but the film defends the defiance.

title: Doctor Laennec
text: A medical biography of René Laennec, the inventor of the stethoscope, covering his work on consumption, his rivals, his marriage and his death in Brittany. Laennec was a devout Catholic, but no synopsis or listing mentions faith as part of the film.

title: Don Lorenzo
text: A musical crime melodrama built as a vehicle for the singer Luciano Tajoli. Don Lorenzo, a former army chaplain, runs a village for the unemployed. His charity frames the story, but the plot is about theft, a wrongful arrest and a girl's suicide attempt.

title: The Nuns' Boy
text: A bullfighting melodrama. A foundling left at a convent door is entrusted by the nuns to a gardener who passes on his love of the bulls, and the boy grows up wanting to be a matador. The convent is the starting point, the bullring the subject.

title: The Sanctuary Does Not Surrender
text: A Civil War siege film about the Civil Guards and civilians who held the shrine of Our Lady of la Cabeza in 1936-37. The shrine is the setting and the cause political: the account found records no priest, Mass, prayer or devotion.

title: End of a Priest
text: A Czech film in which a bumbling sexton poses as a priest, hears confessions and gives last rites, and is denounced by the atheist schoolmaster. The national film archive reads it as an allegory of totalitarianism. The sacraments are the premise of a comedy.

title: Brother Bullfighter
text: A farce in which a friar, played by the bullfighter Paco Camino, enters the ring to save his convent's finances and attracts a woman's interest. The convent is the setting for a bullfighting comedy, and no faith, sacrament or saint is at its centre.

title: Frei Luís de Sousa
text: A faithful screen version of Almeida Garrett's Romantic tragedy. A first husband lost at Alcácer-Quibir returns after twenty years and the second marriage is undone. The couple take the habit at the end, but the subject is fate and family honour, not the faith.

title: Full of Grace
text: A film on Our Lady's last years, with Peter at her side. He is told he is following, not leading, which sets aside the primacy, and her death and burial are shown with no sign of the Assumption. Both points count against it.

title: The Last Ones
text: A stark portrait of peasant poverty under Fascism, drawn from the childhood of the Servite Fr David Turoldo, who co-directed. The film itself is a rural social drama, with no discussion of faith or the Church.

title: Hope: Our Lady of Knock
text: An EWTN docudrama on the apparition of 1879. The reenacted first half is not objectionable, but the second turns to the shrine's present life: modern pilgrims' testimonies and a recent cure, with the shrine's rector and officials as interpreters. The post-conciliar Church is its frame.

title: The Forbidden Christ
text: Malaparte's postwar revenge drama, a parable in which a carpenter falsely confesses and dies in a guilty man's place. The religious meaning is carried by an invented village rite and a Christ-figure, not by Catholic practice. The Legion of Decency rated it B.

title: Sister Dulce
text: Irmã Dulce was beatified in 2011 and canonised in 2019, and had no recognition before the Council.

title: Jasminum
text: A magic-realist comedy set in a Camaldolese monastery whose monks are named for the scents they give off. Religious life is the setting, the monks are comic figures, and the plot turns on a restorer's alchemical experiments and a love elixir.

title: Our Lady of Sorrows
text: From a zarzuela in which a painter turned monk meets again the woman who left him, now abandoned with a child. He leaves the monastery and renounces his vows to marry her. The happy ending is the abandonment of religious life.

title: The Holy War
text: A Mexican film on the Cristero War. A reference summary says it shows clerical groups, in fanatical opposition to President Calles, manipulating peasants in 1927. That is an anticlerical thesis about the Cristero War.

title: Sister San Sulpicio
text: A silent comedy from Palacio Valdés's novel. A Galician doctor falls for a lively young Andalusian nun, who leaves the convent and marries him. Religious life is the obstacle in a romance, not the film's subject.

title: Sister San Sulpicio
text: A sound remake of Rey's 1927 comedy, with Imperio Argentina as the singing young nun with whom Dr Sanjurjo falls in love at a spa. As in the novel, she leaves the convent for marriage. The convent is the comic obstacle in a romance.

title: Sister San Sulpicio
text: A Carmen Sevilla romantic comedy from Palacio Valdés's novel. A lively Andalusian girl becomes a nun, is posted to a sanatorium and falls in love with its doctor. Her habit is the comic impediment to marriage, not the subject.

title: The Prayer
text: A French drama set in a lay community modelled on the Cenacolo, founded in 1983, with post-conciliar prayer and liturgy as the normal pattern. The film leaves its faith deliberately open, and a nun is shown in a fascistic light. The setting is Catholic; the faith is not the subject.

title: Hoboes in Paradise
text: A French comedy condemned by the National Legion of Decency (C). It found that the story, though presented as folklore, ridicules religious characters and practices, and that it contains immodest costuming and condones immoral actions.

title: Letters from My Windmill
text: Pagnol's adaptation of Daudet's tales. The Legion of Decency condemned it (C) because two episodes, the three low Masses and Father Gaucher's elixir, treat religion and religious characters in a frivolous, disrespectful and grossly comical way. The third episode is not religious.

title: Love and Mercy: Faustina
text: St Faustina Kowalska was beatified in 1993 and canonised in 2000, and the film ends with her beatification. Her writings were also under a Holy Office ban from 1959 to 1978.

title: My Son Ceferino Namuncurá
text: Ceferino Namuncurá, the Mapuche Salesian pupil, was declared Venerable in 1972 and beatified only in 2007.

title: The Monastery of Santa Chiara
text: A Neapolitan war melodrama in which a Jewish nightclub singer, helped by her SS-officer lover, hides in a monastery. The monastery is a hiding place, not the subject. Nothing in the sources makes religious life or the faith central.

title: The Eyes of Asia
text: Its protagonist, the Jesuit Julião Nakaura, is recognised as blessed only through the beatification of Peter Kibe and 187 companions in 2008. The rule decides it, whatever one makes of the film's apostasy theme.

title: Father Rupert Mayer
text: Rupert Mayer was beatified in 1987. Before that he was only a Servant of God, which is not recognition as blessed.

title: Forbidden Priests
text: A priest in 1940, played by Robert Hossein, has a relationship with a young woman, fathers a child and later becomes a communist. The script is co-written by a former priest and the premise argues against clerical celibacy. A priest's failure is its thesis, not a failure it judges.

title: Righteous Stepinac
text: A documentary devoted to Cardinal Alojzije Stepinac, who was beatified in 1998 with no earlier title.

title: Saints and Sinners
text: An Irish-village comedy-drama from Paul Vincent Carroll's play. A man is wrongly accused of theft, there is a romance, and a village prophetess predicts the end of the world. The Canon is a well-played supporting figure, but the story is Irish whimsy, not a Catholic subject.

title: St. Peter's Umbrella
text: A Hungarian-Czechoslovak version of Mikszáth's comic novel. The village believes St Peter left an umbrella, but the plot is a lawyer's hunt for it and his love for a girl. The miracle is a mistaken attribution, and folk piety is colour, not subject.
